$note: FIELDWORKS rules, version 3 (the rework, design D34; version 3 adds the feel pass: moves, machines, bosses, run upgrades, what play score opens, the worlds, hard mode, sound and the embed) — the owner's instance as the first of the template. Every number the engine, the castle module and the prototype read lives here; the code carries none of its own except the hash and the fight's fixed step. Re-theme by writing another file; re-balance by editing this one and running the sim. The bank is the game's every sentence, seeded once for the owner's review (D14) and then data. Public-tier text only: ward names come from the public project seed at run time, never from here.

save.$note: The device keeps the journal (which evidence it has seen and shown), the horde clock and its history, the play scores and the paint (key fieldworks-save). It keeps no map: the castle is derived from the evidence each time. A save carries this version and a hash of the rules it was made under; another rules hash loads under the current rules and says so once; a version-1 save (the old fortress map) keeps its journal and says so once; an unreadable save is discarded and the castle still stands on its evidence (pillar 2). Version 3 of the rules adds to the play record a lifetime play score (what it opens is for play only), the mute and hard-mode switches and two counts; an older play record starts its lifetime score at its bests. Embedded in a host app the device keeps the play record alone, under its own key (fieldworks-embed-play): nothing about the world is stored. Version 3 also journals every day's bounty pick (ids only, never pruned: the bonus on a drop must outlive any window) beside the horde clock, and the play record stores the gear the player chose per slot as a hash, never an item id (so the choice is on the device, in the play save, embedded too). Embedded, only the host's picks are used and they are not stored.

clock.$note: The horde clock runs on real days (D25, re-cut by D34): a warning warning_hours ahead and an arrival at horde.arrive_hour in the device's own zone. The prototype steps the day from its dev bar so a horde can be met in a five-minute session. The prototype's clock is day-granular: horde.arrive_hour is the app's, and nothing here reads it yet.

states.$note: Honest states, each reachable from the dev bar: an unread backlog leaves the horde clock unlit (it gathers nothing, never a zero); a dark lane draws from its last read and says how old it is; a quiet week dims the beacon.

onboarding.$note: Three cards on the first open (key fieldworks-onboarded), replayable from the dev bar. The words are in the bank.

telemetry.$note: Local only (key fieldworks-telemetry). Shown on the Keeper screen; never sent.

castle.$note: The castle (D34, D37–D39). It is a fold over the evidence log and nothing else: a piece per evidence event, by the event's kind first, else by its drop's grade. Nothing here is bought, placed or lost. Tower points fill the slots breadth-first.

horde.$note: The horde (D34, D40–D42). It gathers from the aged backlog (the engine's siege count), is announced warning_hours ahead, and never comes inside min_gap_days of the last. Its size is the backlog that day plus how many came before; its bosses are the siege engines. The fight is one stepping function (src/castle.js), so the forecast is the fight without the Keeper. Every piece the evidence lands between the warning and the arrival rallies the castle for that fight (rally). A horde takes nothing: a breach dims the walls until the next evidence.

stage.$note: The stages (D34, D43–D46) and the feel pass (version 3): a side-scrolling run for each stated week of the plan (positions, never a title) and one free-standing endless stage. Everything here is play. A kill, a spark, a boss and a cleared stage pay play score, never XP, a level, an item or a castle piece. Lifetime play score opens things for PLAY (more of the upgrade pool, a second jump, a starting pick, worlds for the Wilds) and paint; a run's upgrades last for the run. The Keeper's hull grows with the evidence level. Nothing a run does can take anything.

meta.$note: What lifetime play score opens, for good: more of the run-upgrade pool, a second jump, a starting pick, worlds for the Wilds. All of it is for play. None of it is XP, a level, an item or a castle piece, and a death takes none of it.

embed.$note: The embeddable build (embed/play.js) in a host app's same-origin frame. The world arrives by postMessage and is never stored; if none arrives in wait_ms the game plays signed out. The embed's save holds play only.

audio.$note: Sound is made in code (WebAudio): no audio file. An effect is a swept tone (from → to Hz over s seconds), optionally with a noise burst, or a run of MIDI notes; a song is a lead and a bass line in sixteenth steps (MIDI numbers in one string, 0 a rest), looped. Nothing plays before the first input; mute is remembered in the play record.

gear.$note: Gear (FW2, D52). A drop is gear by its grade: the kind of event that dropped it gives the slot (a close the blaster, a task the visor, a lesson the boots, a lift the plating, a decision the core), its grade the power; a sealed item is gear in the same slot. The Keeper carries one piece per slot, equipped from the archive. Nothing is spent, moved or lost by equipping, and play never adds a piece: gear exists only because evidence dropped an item. A sealed item is gear with no name. What gear does is for play: it never yields XP, a level, an item or a castle piece. 'chosen' is stored as a hash of the item id, never the id.

bounty.$note: Today's bounty (FW2, D61): one open public order picked by rule, oldest first, then the highest Pn (P0 first), then the quickest (a decision counts as one step, else its step count), then the id. A private order is never the bounty. Closing the bounty on its own day adds score_bonus to the drop's rarity score. The bonus is added on the day and never removed on another; no close is ever worth less for it. The pick that made a bonus is evidence: it is kept for as long as the item is (the journal never prunes it; embedded, the host sends every day it holds), and without a host's pick nothing is ever computed embedded, so no bonus can later be lost.

input.$note: FW10 (design D67, D79): the touch input. One canvas takes every pointer; a stick floats where the left thumb lands; the right side is drawn buttons that tile it with no gap. Sizes in CSS pixels; positions as fractions of the surface.
